questions.title: Errno After Successful Call
questions.description: Why must a C program set errno to 0 BEFORE calling a library function whose failure it wants to detect via errno?
questions.Option1: Because errno is undefined until explicitly initialized
questions.Option2: Because a successful library call does not reset errno, so a stale value from a previous failed call could be misread as a new error
questions.Option3: Because errno is thread-local and must be reset per-thread
questions.Option4: Because errno must always be 0 at function entry
